question: Should OpenClaw support one validated immediate `.openclaw` symlink as a public exec-approvals state layout, and require Node/macOS to enforce the same contract?
rationale: Current main intentionally rejects this path shape after the narrower predecessor, while this branch expands the accepted local trust boundary in two independent runtimes; that acceptance policy cannot be selected safely from tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow supported layout
options.body: Approve exactly one documented first-level symlink shape, then require a fresh rebase, shared-or-equivalent invariants, and real macOS/node-host acceptance and rejection proof.

options.title: Keep the strict current layout
options.body: Retain the existing symlink rejection policy and close this PR and its linked request as an unsupported state-directory topology.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow supported layout
recommendation.body: Approve exactly one documented first-level symlink shape, then require a fresh rebase, shared-or-equivalent invariants, and real macOS/node-host acceptance and rejection proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current merged symlink exception and are the strongest history-based routing candidate for deciding whether its scope should expand.
